summary: The three edges at a 20 mm cube's corner rounded 20, as wide as the faces, must be refused as too large, so a fit can reduce them (PR #477, which refs #293; the fin case of #293 is 293-fin-round-past-its-thickness). Each round's corner end lies r from the corner along its edge, so at r 20 the corner takes the whole of every edge. SolidCraft refuses it and its fit_max reduces it to 19.99. The pinned SMLib refuses it too, with no size. With the generic blend's step 6 (the cliff overflow trimmed at its creases, fillet_overflow_trim_at_creases) and step 5's sizes, the trim refuses it because the corners take the whole edge, and it reports the largest radius that builds: the edge length over the corner's take per unit radius, 20 / 1, less the fit margin of a thousand edge tolerances (1e-5), 19.99. The fork's capi test scenario_cube_corner_rounds_as_wide_as_faces_refused expects the same, and a local build of tangency-labs/smlib 5e8c9c1 reports 19.989999999999998. Built at that fit, the rounds take 3 (1 - pi/4) r^2 (20 - r) along the edges past the corner cube and r^3 (1 - pi/6) from the cube less its sphere octant (SolidCraft's closed form; it checked 2e-4 relative on a mesh, this checks 1e-4 mm^3).
